comments.text:
I'm 30 now and I have a wife. It was awful. I have my own situation where our apartment was flooded in 2023 because the water company didn't repair a broken line in time and because they were a govt. contract, none of us in the complex could sue. Then our insurance wouldn't help us and we spent ~$5K JUST to clean up the mess. We never got compensation for the (insurance estimated) $10K< in damages because they claimed something in the policy that just wasn't there, and no lawyer would return emails or calls. We moved into a new apartment, but that now cost us an extra $300/month. That also all happened right after I got fired. Thankfully it was stupid and I got a severance, but that was still only $3K, so we blew through that fast. Then, when I started my new job I got sick with Covid. I should mention, up until this point, we combined for ~$100K each of the last 3 years. That was at the end of Aug. 2023. In September off that year, I  was diagnosed with Long Covid. I've been in an out of work (thankfully paid for the most part) since. I am finally at the point where I can TRY to work again. I have not been fired, though, that is not without my company trying. Since then all my peers/coworkers have been getting raises on their base pay (I'm in sales) and I've been stuck at the original pay. I also have only been paid $33K this year because of my disability claims. I can also say I got sick at work during the return to work, but I don't have a case legally because judges decided that we can't track it, even though my company already does and put out a warning via email about a Covid outbreak.

Anyways, my point isn't to dump trauma, the point is to illustrate that we all have struggles and not everyone is going to give their story. Each and every one of us has our own shit to deal with, and that's before considering the economy or anything else. But yeah, eventually, we couldn't afford the apartment, and with the effective paycut because of my disability - and going months without pay. We now live with my parents and are starting to save for a house in case (really, if and only if) the bubble bursts. we also racked up $19K in credit card dept trying to keep from drowning.
